gen-dafont-amadeus-fs-paquito: Wide, stretched-out words with round letters that carry no tilt: that is Amadeus, set over the low, friendly Paquito. Its low x-height-to-cap gap is the quality that sticks.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, its lowercase sitting barely below the capitals. Early GameBoy up top shifts its stroke weight noticeably but never dramatically, so over a longer stretch Paquito keeps feeling like one friendly voice.

gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-paquito: Cosmic and loose, Galaxy gives every curve and straight a single width with plenty of breathing space around it. Paquito, a text serif, counters with a low, approachable gap between lowercase and caps.

gen-dafont-joystix-fs-paquito: Bold arcade energy comes from Joystix, its widely tracked letters showing a faint crayon-like rhythm. And Paquito, a classic serif, follows in a confident, approachable voice that would stay easy over a long page.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-fs-paquito: Towering lowercase, one character per beat: that is Minecraftia, with dark swollen strokes beside hairline-thin ones. And Paquito, a text serif, steps in lower and friendlier, so the two share a line without crowding.
